reviewer.subagents: Three subagents drafted groups 1–3. The lead reviewer drafted group 4. Each group then received a second reading by a different reviewer. The lead editor assembled and validated both formats.

segments.sense: A compact title announcing a precise, clear summary of music, here.

best_ru.why: The verbal title conveys the compendious character of summa and marks the supplied noun.

best_en.why: “Precise and lucid summary” gives both adjectives their natural force in a title.

notes_to_keep.gist: The heading supplies no author's name. The running title COMPENDIVM on the facing page helps explain summa.

segments.sense: The ancients said that music holds this universe together: nothing in nature subsists without commensuration and proportion.

text_issues_review.printed: VNiuersum hoc, antiqui Musica / contineri perhibuerunt. Nihil e- / nim in rerum natura absque com- / mensuratione et proportione con- / sistit: neque quicquam eorum quæ
text_issues_review.proposal: Эта вселенная, как утверждали древние, заключена в музыке. / This universe, the ancients declared, is contained in music.
text_issues_review.why: The bare ablative gives the means by which things hold together. X04 calls music the universe’s harmony and X07 describes it ordering all things. Spatial enclosure obscures that argument.

best_ru.why: The active construction makes the cosmic function of music immediately intelligible.

best_en.why: Preserves both members of the recurring pair and the opening emphasis on the universe.

notes_to_keep.gist: Keep the lexical distinction between commensuratio, proportio and the proportionalitas of X04, especially ahead of the numerical use of proportio.

segments.sense: Nothing that comes about without due commensuration and proportion is said to have been rightly produced or born, whether by art or nature, whether perceived by sense or by intellect alone.

errors.quote: ничто из того, что возникает, нельзя назвать
errors.problem: The initial nominative-sounding ничто jars with the impersonal нельзя назвать.
errors.fix: Use «ни о чём из возникающего нельзя сказать» or «ничего из того, что возникает, нельзя назвать».

best_ru.why: The restrictions of the conditional and both pairs of alternatives are clear in idiomatic Russian.

best_en.why: The relative clause preserves the condition without suspending the governing verb across a long parenthesis.

segments.sense: Music itself, taken in its own right, is indeed a kind of commensuration and proportionality, since it is the harmony of the universe.

divergences.issue: Does omnino mark extent or assent?

readings.construal: Entirely, altogether.

divergences.verdict: The extensive sense of omnino is well attested. Lewis and Short also gives an assertive force, especially in concessions. In this positive assertion quaedam qualifies the kind of commensuration and nimirum introduces a further affirmation. ‘Certainly a kind’ reads naturally; ‘altogether’ is defensible if it qualifies the identification as a whole.

text_issues_review.printed: Cæterùm Musica ipsa per se commensura- / tio quædam omnino et proportionalitas est, ni- / mirum harmonia uniuersi existens. Fortassis et
text_issues_review.proposal: Сама музыка по себе во всех отношениях есть своего рода соразмерность и пропорциональность. / Music itself is in every respect a kind of commensurateness and proportionality.
text_issues_review.why: The extensive force is lexical, although the assertive force sits more naturally with quaedam.

best_ru.why: Keeps ipsa per se and separates the assertion from the explanatory clause.

best_en.why: Distinguishes proportionality from proportion and reads omnino naturally with the assertion.

notes_to_keep.gist: Proportionalitas replaces proportio in X04. The terminological shift can be retained without insisting that the author here specifies a relation between two ratios.

editor_questions: Should omnino mark assent or extent in the definition?

errors.fix: even the divine nature itself

errors.problem: In the English, ‘itself’ renders ipsam, but the additive et (‘even/also’) has no counterpart.

best_en.why: Attuned and fitted differentiate the two verbs, with videtur and the superlative intact.

notes_to_keep.gist: The pair concinnare/coaptare prepares the account of musical fitting in X12. Keep the difference visible alongside the technical consonantia.

errors.fix: “Such, evidently, was the wonder they thought music deserved.”

errors.problem: An indefinite wonder suggests a remarkable object and obscures the attitude expressed by dignari.
errors.fix: “Such, indeed, was the wonder they thought music deserved.”

errors.problem: The English omits nimirum, which emphasizes the inference drawn from the preceding description.
errors.fix: Such, evidently, was the wonder they thought music deserved.

errors.quote: Such was the wonder they thought music deserved.

text_issues_review.printed: optimè se habere uidetur. Tanto nimirum Mu- / sicam illi dignati sunt miraculo. Ea quando in
text_issues_review.proposal: ‘honoured music with so great admiration’
text_issues_review.why: Dignari takes what someone is judged worthy of in the ablative. Wonder as the response of the ancients gives a coherent compliment to music. An object of marvel does not fit as well after ‘worthy of’.

best_ru.why: Miraculo is the admiration accorded, and разумеется reflects nimirum.

best_en.why: Both give the same idiomatic expression for the ancients’ wonder.

notes_to_keep.gist: The construction with miraculum can express an observer’s wonder. Pliny’s tree worthy of marvel supplies a useful comparison.

segments.sense: Music is discernible in everything, regulates and adorns all, and gives pleasure to sense, congruence (harmony) to nature, and blessedness to intellect. We shall speak briefly of music as considered by the senses, more precisely by hearing.

divergences.issue: Is music perceived or considered under the aspect of sense?

readings.construal: The subject is considered or examined in, or through, the senses.

quotes.ru: которая рассматривается в чувствах
quotes.en: which is considered in the senses

readings.construal: The subject is perceived by the senses.

quotes.ru: которую воспринимают чувствами
quotes.en: that is perceived by the senses

divergences.verdict: Consideratur can mean observed or perceived, as Lewis and Short records, as well as considered intellectually. The coming exposition and the limitation to one sense favour ‘examined through hearing’. D emphasizes the sensory object and is defensible in this setting.
divergences.recommended_ru: о той музыке, которую рассматривают с точки зрения чувственного восприятия, вернее, слуха
divergences.recommended_en: the music studied through the senses, or rather through one of them, hearing

errors.quote: the one sense of hearing
errors.problem: The genitive plural sensuum marks hearing as one of the senses. ‘The one sense of hearing’ blurs the selection from that plurality.
errors.fix: one of the senses, hearing

text_issues_review.printed: sicam illi dignati sunt miraculo. Ea quando in / omnibus conspicitur, atque uniuersa temperat, e- / xornatqúe, tum sensui uoluptatem, congruentiam / autem (harmoniam dico) Naturæ, beatitatem / denique intellectui largitur: nos de ea Musica quæ / in sensibus, aut potius uno sensuum auditu con- / sideratur, paucis disseremus.
text_issues_review.proposal: ‘since it... and bestows’ / ‘when it..., then it bestows’
text_issues_review.why: Quando and tum can form a temporal correlation, but the universal claims describe a standing relation. Causal quando better introduces the decision to discuss audible music.
evidence: Lewis & Short, s.v. quando, temporal and causal conjunction [checked]

best_ru.why: Communicates the three recipients and their gifts clearly and translates temperat in context.

best_en.why: Connects all three gifts with the causal introduction and preserves music as an object of consideration.

notes_to_keep.gist: Congruentia is glossed as harmonia here. Vinet uses convenientia at the corresponding point.

segments.sense: A note is the pitch or tenor of a voice undivided by any interval, capable of participating in harmony. The placement of the genitive and of particeps allows more than one attachment.

divergences.issue: What do the two near-equivalents designate?

readings.construal: Tension or an act of holding.

quotes.ru: напряжение, или удержание
quotes.en: a tension, or sustained holding

readings.construal: Tension or pitch.

quotes.ru: напряжение, или высота
quotes.en: the tension, or pitch

readings.construal: The pitch or sustained tone of a voice.

quotes.ru: высота, или выдерживаемый тон
quotes.en: a pitch, or sustained tone

quotes.ru: высота голоса
quotes.en: the pitch, or steady tone

divergences.verdict: A note here has a determinate pitch. The etymological idea of tension belongs in an explanatory note. Tenor can describe a sustained course and a vocal tone. No separate pitch interval arises while it is held.
divergences.recommended_en: the pitch, or sustained tone, of a voice
evidence: Boethius, De institutione musica I.8, Friedlein p. 195 [checked]

errors.quote: напряжение, или удержание, голоса / a tension, or sustained holding, of a voice
errors.problem: ‘Tension’ is historically intelligible, and ‘undivided by any interval’ limits the voice to a single level. The combination with ‘holding’ leaves the primary musical quantity, pitch, hard to recognize in both languages.
errors.fix: Use «высота, или выдерживаемый тон» / “pitch, or sustained tone”.

text_issues_review.printed: Sonus est, uocis nullo interuallo diuisæ har- / moniæ particeps intensio, seu tenor. Interuallum
text_issues_review.proposal: Звук есть напряжение, или удержание, голоса, причастное гармонии, не разделённой никаким интервалом. / A note is a tension, or sustained holding, of the voice that partakes of a harmony divided by no interval.
text_issues_review.why: Divisae could agree in form with either genitive, but X12 makes the individual note indivisible. Moreover the English alternative makes the voice participate, although particeps is nominative, not genitive participis. X11 defines harmony as a construction of systems.
evidence: Boethius, De institutione musica I.8, Friedlein p. 195 [checked]

text_issues_review.printed: Sonus est, uocis nullo interuallo diuisæ har- / moniæ particeps intensio, seu tenor. Interuallum
text_issues_review.proposal: Звук — причастная гармонии высота, или устойчивый уровень высоты, голосового звучания, не разделённого никаким интервалом. / A note is a pitch, or steady level of pitch, of vocal sound undivided by any interval, which participates in harmony.
text_issues_review.why: A steady pitch level is an intelligible result of holding the voice. Preserve participation in harmony as a property of the pitch.
evidence: Boethius, De institutione musica I.8, Friedlein p. 195 [checked]

best_ru.why: Names the musical quantity as pitch and keeps the qualifier on that pitch.

best_en.why: “Pitch, or steady tone” makes the paired definition intelligible and resolves the attachment.

notes_to_keep.gist: Use the three distinctions in the note: a single pitch, absence of internal interval, and capacity to be fitted to another note. Boethius I.8 supplies a close Latin parallel.

segments.sense: An interval is the mutual relation or reference of notes, one to another.

errors.quote: a double rendering of one term
errors.problem: Sive presents respectus as a gloss of ratio in this Latin. The claim that a single word underlies them cannot be verified from this version.
errors.fix: Describe Xylander's alternative expressions. The conjecture about the underlying wording is not verified.

best_ru.why: Makes the relation between two notes explicit without tortuous word order.

best_en.why: Places the two notes on either side of the ratio and retains the broader gloss ‘relation’.

notes_to_keep.gist: Here respectus glosses ratio. Vinet’s word in the corresponding definition is habitudo.

segments.sense: A system is a definite combination of intervals.

text_issues_review.printed: siue respectus. Systema, complexus est certus / interuallorum. Harmonia, ipsa constructio sy-
text_issues_review.proposal: Система — некое сочетание интервалов. / A system is a certain combination of intervals.
text_issues_review.why: An unspecified but particular combination is possible. Certus more naturally indicates that the combination has a determinate constitution.

best_ru.why: The three texts coincide and render the definite combination succinctly.

best_en.why: The three texts give the same precise definition.

segments.sense: Harmony is the very construction of systems.

best_ru.why: All four give the same Russian definition and retain ipsa.

best_en.why: The identical phrase ‘the very construction’ reproduces the emphasis of ipsa.

notes_to_keep.gist: The construction of systems anticipates X45–47, where their combination is described as the work of harmony.

segments.sense: A note admits no division, any more than a geometrical point. Its utterance can be fitted harmoniously to another note, hence the qualification about participation in harmony.

best_ru.why: Connects the note’s indivisibility with the geometrical point, then explains its relation to a second note.

best_en.why: “Sounded” and “fitted to another note” give precise, natural musical English.

notes_to_keep.gist: Euclid’s definition of the point explains the comparison: the object is defined as having no part.

segments.sense: Otherwise it would be a dissonant, unconsonant note, indeed mere noise emitted at random and of no use for consonance.

errors.quote: dissonant, with no consonance
errors.problem: The paired adjectives dissonus and non consonus both predicate a quality of the note. The second adjective has become a free-standing abstract noun.
errors.fix: dissonant, not consonant

best_ru.why: Clearly separates the two adjectives and the stronger exclusion of mere noise.

best_en.why: Preserves the conditional force of sit and the future dicetur and distinguishes sonus from strepitus.

notes_to_keep.gist: The contrast limits the technical sonus to something that can participate in harmony. Strepitus describes the excluded noise.

segments.sense: These note species complete a heccaedecachord, glossed as a sixteen-string instrument, in an instrument fitted with fifteen strings (Greek pentecaedecachord). The octave’s end is taken straight on as the beginning of what follows.

divergences.issue: Does the unusual first name designate an instrument or a separate theoretical system?

readings.construal: A transliterated instrument name followed by its Latin gloss.

quotes.ru: геккайдекахорд, то есть инструмент о шестнадцати струнах
quotes.en: the hekkaidekachord, that is, the instrument of sixteen strings

quotes.ru: геккайдекахорд, то есть инструмент из шестнадцати струн

divergences.verdict: Hoc est expressly defines an instrument. The two octachords do furnish a theoretical sixteen-place scheme, but the passage exploits a difference between separately counted and physically present strings. Keeping the name and the immediate gloss makes the wordplay intelligible.
divergences.recommended_ru: геккайдекахорд, то есть инструмент с шестнадцатью струнами

errors.quote: шестнадцатиструнную систему / a sixteen-string system
errors.problem: System is an interpretation absent from Xylander’s own gloss instrumentum.
errors.fix: Retain the name, explain the count in the note.

errors.problem: In context the colon is intended to link note positions, but the bare equality reads as an equality of numbers, which fails by cross-multiplication. The underlying octave spans are correct.
errors.fix: Write ‘note 1 is to note 8 as note 8 is to note 15’ or give the two equal octave frequency ratios.

text_issues_review.printed: perbolæon. Per has sonorum species heccæde / cachordum, hoc est, sedecim chordarum instru- / mentum in quindecim fidibus instructo organo / (Pentecædecachordum uocant Græci) absol- / uitur, fine octachordi ad principium sequentium / continuò assumpto. Quam enim rationem ha-
text_issues_review.proposal: ‘taken in continuity to the beginning of the following [strings]’
text_issues_review.why: Sequentium is plural and can refer to the ensuing notes or strings. The grave accent in the page image favors adverbial continuo. The shared endpoint makes continuity of succession pertinent.
evidence: Boethius, De institutione musica I.20, Friedlein p. 207, counting mese twice [checked]

text_issues_review.printed: perbolæon. Per has sonorum species heccæde / cachordum, hoc est, sedecim chordarum instru- / mentum in quindecim fidibus instructo organo / (Pentecædecachordum uocant Græci) absol- / uitur, fine octachordi ad principium sequentium / continuò assumpto. Quam enim rationem ha-
text_issues_review.proposal: конец октахорда сразу принимают за начало следующих [октахордов] / the end of the octachord being taken immediately as the beginning of the [octachords] that follow
text_issues_review.why: Only one ensuing octachord is at stake in a two-octave system. The proposed plural ‘octachords’ has no support in the count; a series of notes does.
evidence: Boethius, De institutione musica I.20, Friedlein p. 207, counting mese twice [checked]

text_issues_review.printed: Per has sonorum species
text_issues_review.proposal: «посредством этих видов звуков» / 'through these species of notes'; «посредством этих звуков» / 'by means of these notes'.
text_issues_review.why: Omitting species erases Xylander's explicit classification after the enumeration of named notes. ‘These kinds of notes’ keeps both words.
evidence: Xyl. 41.25–42.5 (Basel 1556, page image and printed lines) [checked]

best_ru.why: Keeps both instrument names, the count of strings and the bracketed head supplied to sequentium.

best_en.why: Retains and glosses the two instrument names while identifying the shared octachord boundary.

notes_to_keep.gist: Two octachords yield sixteen counted places and fifteen distinct strings, since the eighth note ends the first and begins the second. Keep this explanation apart from the erroneous numerical equality in the check.

segments.sense: The first note stands to the eighth in the same ratio as the eighth to the fifteenth.

errors.quote: 1st : 8th = octave, 2:1

errors.fix: Distinguish string lengths, ordered frequencies, and the ascending interval multiplier.

errors.quote: 1 : 15 = double octave, 4:1
errors.problem: The numerals identify scale positions, and the high-to-low frequency ratio or low-to-high length ratio is 4:1. As written the equality looks arithmetical.
errors.fix: Write ‘the first and fifteenth notes span a double octave’ and specify the orientation of any ratio.

best_ru.why: The two parallel relations read naturally and occur in the order of the Latin.

best_en.why: “Stands in the same ratio” relates the notes rather than their position numbers.

notes_to_keep.gist: Both spans encompass seven steps. Their ascending multipliers are 2 and 2, whereas frequencies ordered first-to-eighth and eighth-to-fifteenth give 1:2 each.

segments.sense: Paraphony and antiphony, glossed as sounding alongside and sounding opposite, differ in time. The eighth with the first, eleventh with fourth, twelfth with fifth and fifteenth with eighth ascend or descend alike as pitch is raised or lowered, low notes answering high proportionally or conversely.

segments.sense: These ratios were discovered through differences in string length or thickness, through tension produced by turning the pegs, or perhaps more clearly through the pull of weights. divergences.issue: Is a particular dimension of the cavity meant?

readings.construal: Size or capacity of the cavity.

editor_questions: Is there sufficient reason to identify the dimension of the cavity as its width?

segments.sense: Among systems, the four-string tetrachord encompasses the full power of the fourth, the five-string pentachord the full capacity of the fifth, and the eight-string octachord all the material of the octave. A further system of sixteen consecutive strings encompasses the whole range of the double octave, now called a fifteenth. It serves two uses because it comprises the foregoing intervals and their compounds.

divergences.issue: Is materies literal matter or the contents of the octave?

readings.construal: Use the literal matter or material.

quotes.ru: третья — октахорд, построенный из восьми струн и объемлющий всю материю октавы.
quotes.en: another the octachord, constructed of eight strings, encompassing the whole matter of the octave.

quotes.ru: Ещё одна — октахорд, построенный из восьми струн и охватывающий всю материю октавы.
quotes.en: Another is the octachord, built from eight strings and encompassing the whole material of the octave.

quotes.ru: ещё одна — октахорд, построенный из восьми струн и объемлющий всю материю октавы.
quotes.en: another the octachord, constructed of eight strings, encompassing the whole matter of the octave.

readings.construal: Uses content.

quotes.ru: Ещё одна — октахорд, построенный из восьми струн и охватывающий всё содержание октавы.
quotes.en: Another is the octachord, built of eight strings and encompassing the entire content of the octave.

divergences.verdict: Materies is one of four varied expressions for what these systems contain. ‘Content’ is apt here, but ‘material’ better prepares materia in X43. Both can be defended.
divergences.recommended_en: encompassing the entire material of the octave
evidence: Lewis and Short, s.v. materia [from memory]

text_issues_review.printed: continentib. sedecim neruis

notes_to_keep.gist: Two octachords sharing their boundary yield fifteen distinct positions, yet this particular sentence says sixteen consecutive strings. The parenthetic contemporary name ‘fifteenth’ sharpens the difficulty.

editor_questions: Should matter/material be carried from X42 into X43, or should X42 use ‘content’ with a note?

segments.sense: Systems and the intervals conceived between or within them differ in this respect: the entire constitution of systems is considered in matter, while intervals are understood by mentally abstracting matter.

divergences.issue: Are intervals contained or conceived within systems?

readings.construal: Contained or comprised within.

quotes.ru: Между системами, стало быть, и интервалами, заключёнными внутри них, различие то, что всякое устроение систем усматривается в материи, интервалы же мыслятся, когда материя отделена мыслью.
quotes.en: Between systems, accordingly, and the intervals contained in their midst there is this difference:

quotes.en: Systems accordingly differ from the intervals comprised within them in that the whole constitution of a system is observed in matter, whereas intervals are understood by setting matter aside in thought.

quotes.ru: Итак, между системами и интервалами, заключёнными внутри них, та разница, что всякое устроение систем рассматривается в материи, а интервалы постигаются, когда материя отделена мыслью.

divergences.recommended_en: the intervals conceived within the systems
evidence: Lewis and Short, s.v. concipio [from memory]

divergences.issue: Every instance, or the entirety of a structure?

readings.construal: Every constitution.

quotes.ru: Между системами, стало быть, и интервалами, заключёнными внутри них, различие то, что всякое устроение систем усматривается в материи, интервалы же мыслятся, когда материя отделена мыслью.

quotes.ru: Итак, системы отличаются от заключённых в них интервалов тем, что всё устройство системы рассматривается в материи, а интервалы постигаются в отвлечении от материи.
quotes.en: Systems accordingly differ from the intervals comprised within them in that the whole constitution of a system is observed in matter, whereas intervals are understood by setting matter aside in thought.

quotes.ru: Строение системы во всей его полноте рассматривают в материи, а интервалы постигают, мысленно отвлекаясь от материи.
quotes.en: The whole structure of a system is considered in matter, whereas intervals are grasped by abstracting from matter in thought.

divergences.recommended_en: the whole constitution of systems

text_issues_review.printed: in medio eorum concepta intervalla
text_issues_review.proposal: …между системами и интервалами, мыслимыми внутри них… / …between systems and the intervals conceived within them…

segments.sense: Harmony characteristically constructs these systems and fits them together according to one of the genera of melody. Melody might approximately be called the modulation of song or tune. The genera are diatonic, chromatic and harmonic. The last takes its name from harmony itself.

divergences.issue: What defines melody in the parenthesis?

readings.construal: A measured shaping of song or tune.

quotes.ru: Гармонии свойственно строить и слаживать эти системы сообразно какому-либо из таких родов мелодии (её можно бы приблизительно назвать мерным ведением пения, или напева):
quotes.en: It is proper to harmony to construct and frame those systems according to some one of these genera of melody (you might roughly call it the measured shaping of song, or of a tune), which are the diatonic, the chromatic, and the harmonic, to which the name has fallen from Harmony itself.

readings.construal: The melodic movement of singing or a tune.

quotes.ru: Гармонии свойственно строить и стройно сочетать эти системы сообразно одному из родов мелодии (её можно приблизительно определить как мелодическое движение пения или напева).
quotes.en: It belongs to harmony to construct and arrange these systems according to one of the genera of melody (which one might broadly call the melodic movement of singing or of a tune).

readings.construal: Russian has melodic movement, English ‘modulation’, in a historical sense explained in a note.

quotes.ru: Свойство гармонии — строить и слаживать эти системы применительно к какому-либо из этих родов мелодии (её, пожалуй, можно было бы назвать мелодическим движением пения или напева), каковы диатонический, хроматический и гармонический, которому имя досталось от самой Гармонии.
quotes.en: It is proper to harmony to construct and attune those systems for some one of these genera of melody (you might almost call it the modulation of song or tune), which are the diatonic, the chromatic and the harmonic, to which [last] the name fell from Harmony itself.

readings.construal: The melodic shaping or structure of singing or a tune.

quotes.ru: Гармонии свойственно строить эти системы и согласовывать их с одним из следующих родов мелодии (мелодией, пожалуй, можно назвать мелодический строй пения или напева).
quotes.en: It belongs to harmony to construct these systems and fit them to one of the following genera of melody (one might perhaps describe melody as the melodic shaping of singing or of a tune).

divergences.verdict: All take cantus and cantilenae with modulationem. The pertinent sense is measured or melodic shaping of sound. Unqualified modern ‘modulation’ can evoke change of key, but C explains the older meaning. Preserve the two genitives and the provisional fere.

errors.quote: мерным ведением пения, или напева

text_issues_review.printed: eam cantus seu cantilenae modulationem fere dixeris
text_issues_review.proposal: ‘modulation’ or ‘melodic ordering’

evidence: Xylander, Basel (1556), 47.21–48.1 (page image and diplomatic lines) [checked]

best_ru.why: Separates the three genera from the parenthetic gloss and identifies the final antecedent.

editor_questions: Agree an English rendering for modulatio that will also work elsewhere in Xylander.

segments.sense: If harmony, the fitting together of consonances, moves chiefly by tones, the diatonic genus of melody results. If by semitones, the chromatic, as if one said coloured. If harmony is for the most part realized by dieses, a harmonic song is formed.

errors.quote: гармония большей своей частью выполняется диесами

best_ru.why: Makes the fitting of consonances intelligible, then distinguishes the three ways in which harmony proceeds.

best_en.why: The three parallel conditionals and the coloured gloss are clear.

notes_to_keep.gist: In the fourths that follow, two of the three steps are of the characteristic size. This explains ‘chiefly’ by number of steps rather than by the span they occupy.

segments.sense: Harmony in its entirety cannot be composed exclusively of tones, of semitones, or of dieses.

best_en.why: Accurately distributes ‘alone’ over each of the three interval classes.

segments.sense: The fourth consists of three intervals, namely two tones and a semitone. Once two tones have been fitted into a harmony, the remainder must be completed by a semitone.

quotes.en: But since the fourth consists of three intervals, being comprised, namely, by two tones and a semitone:

quotes.ru: Но так как кварта состоит из трёх интервалов, а именно заключена в двух тонах и полутоне, то, когда в гармонию прилажены два тона, остаток должен быть восполнен полутоном.

readings.construal: Restates the constituents in apposition.

quotes.ru: Но поскольку кварта состоит из трёх интервалов, а именно из двух тонов и полутона, после соединения двух тонов в гармонию остающееся [место] необходимо заполнить полутоном.
quotes.en: But since the fourth consists of three intervals, namely two tones and a semitone, the remainder must be filled with a semitone once two tones have been fitted into the harmony.

readings.construal: The fourth encompasses or spans them.

best_en.why: The English reads continuously from the three constituent intervals to the remaining semitone.

notes_to_keep.gist: At X34 a further quantity was added. Here the two tones leave simply a semitone.

segments.sense: This genus of the fourth is called diatonic, even though a semitone as well as two tones has entered its construction.

best_ru.why: «В его состав … входит» expresses constitution naturally.

best_en.why: The concessive clause identifies the semitone as a constituent despite the genus name.

segments.sense: With two semitones, the interval remaining is formed by coalescence: an incomposite trihemitone.

readings.construal: omits

best_en.why: Keeps both fusion and the incomposite character of the step.

best_ru.why: The emotional effect and comparative degree are explicit.

best_en.why: The blending of the intervals and the power to stir feelings and grief are clear.

notes_to_keep.gist: Xylander stresses efficacy in stirring emotions and grief. Vinet compares the chromatic genus to the preceding genus by its more mournful character.

segments.sense: If the melody proceeds by two dieses, the other interval is a ditone formed by coalescence. This genus of the fourth is called harmonic and, being the best, takes its name from the general word for harmony.

text_issues_review.printed: alterum interuallorum
text_issues_review.proposal: Retain alterum and understand the remaining interval in context.
text_issues_review.why: The scan has alterum. After two dieses at a quarter-tone each, the 2½-tone fourth has one two-tone step left. The two distinct types of step offer a possible binary contrast, but the text does not supply the word ‘types’.
evidence: Xylander, Basel (1556), 48.22–49.1 (page image and diplomatic lines) [checked]

text_issues_review.printed: alterum intervallorum

segments.sense: Innumerable and thoroughly varied kinds of tune arise from changes or differences of intervals, from more oblique or quicker transitions, stays and flows, and from the varied handling of touches and strokes themselves.

notes_to_keep.gist: Vinet introduces two classes without the etymological glosses found in Xylander. His next paragraph illustrates antiphony with octaves.
Boethius reports the Pythagorean objection to the octave plus fourth (8:3) and Ptolemy’s defense of its consonance (De institutione musica II.27 and V.9, ed. Friedlein [checked]).
Pseudo-Aristotle, Problemata XIX.39, 921a [checked], explicitly calls the octave antiphonic and illustrates it with different voices singing together.

Theon gives the same two class names and the four examples C specifies (ed. Hiller, p. 48.16–20 [checked]). Vinet also places the octave plus fourth and octave plus fifth in the antiphonic class. Gaudentius uses paraphonic for intervals between consonance and dissonance and gives the tritone and ditone as examples (Harmonic Introduction 8, ed. Jan, p. 338.3–7 [checked]).

segments.sense: In paraphony the period is unequal, the notes taking one another up smoothly and fittingly in accordance with their proportions and ratios. In antiphony the period is equal: high sounds with low, as eight with one, eleven with four, twelve with five, fifteen with eight. High and low ascend or descend together in equal proportion as pitch is raised or lowered.

term_inconsistencies.problem: The Russian cosmic passages V05, V06 and V08 use согласованность. The same abstract noun at V16 becomes согласование, suggesting the act of bringing into agreement. Retain a noun for the state there, especially as V16 deliberately recalls the opening.

by_translator.strengths: A gives the English editor a good starting point at X13. The change from what a sound might be to what it will be called survives, as does the distinction between a musical note and random noise. The Russian at X26 preserves Xylander’s explicit introduction of composite intervals. A’s commentary also clarifies difficult arithmetic. At X36 and V42 it shows why sixteen contains six twice with two thirds of six left over, and distinguishes that whole ratio from the ratio that follows from a single whole plus two thirds.
by_translator.weaknesses: A sometimes carries the form of the Latin into a modern language at the expense of the sense. At V27 the English says that eight cannot be squared, although the point is that eight is not itself a square number. At V45 the reader has to infer pitch from a bare adjective. The positive cent value in the V22 check belongs to the reciprocal of the indicated ratio. At X38 A’s running translation depends on a conjectural relative pronoun, and the grammatical defense confuses the possible antecedents. The X14 and V17 notes also overstate what distinguishes the name of mese in the lists.

by_translator.strengths: B is especially clear where the argument depends on the direction of a comparison. Both languages preserve the sequence of ratios at V19, the fractional scale values at V22 and the progression from six at X36. The V42 diagram note distinguishes the five printed numerals from the six lines they help explain. The note at X14 helps readers identify unfamiliar pitches while preserving differences between the two lists.
by_translator.weaknesses: Where the naming or the syntax is itself the subject, B can condense too far. Part of X28’s comparison between Greek names and ordinary Latin names becomes tautological in English. The Russian at V09 turns hearing into the human observer’s instrument, and at V14 the wording suggests making the systems that Vinet says are themselves combined. At V32 the language of staying within an interval’s limits obscures the point that the listener hears a single step. At X32 the plural ‘proportions’ also loses B’s earlier distinction between proportio and proportionalitas.

by_translator.strengths: C preserves distinctions on which the argument turns. The English at X02 and V03–V05 makes the common measure audible in two different Latin terms. At V42 both languages make the fractional idiom intelligible, and the Boethian references substantiate it. At V57 both the fusion of the constituents and the description of the result as simple remain in the sentence. C’s comparisons with other theorists are particularly helpful at V38 and V63, where their scope can be checked against the cited passages.
by_translator.weaknesses: C’s explanations sometimes assert more than their evidence supports. At V30 the note identifies a half interval’s ratio with the intermediate length, although the numerical check distinguishes the two. At V31 the note assigns incomposita to the point at which Xylander actually writes compositae. The dating of intensio at V43 is too late, and the note at V46 overlooks the double octave and the eleventh as further decisive tests. At V64 the gender of the three coordinated genre names does not justify the proposed grammatical agreement.

by_translator.strengths: D often supplies a clear running text where a close rendering could obscure the action. At X09 the second expression explains what the mutual relation of notes amounts to. At X42 the description retains sixteen consecutive strings and the name ‘fifteenth’ together. At V14 the systems are the constituents of harmony, and at V43 and V49 pitch movement and compass are intelligible. At V65 the English and Russian make the player’s changes of movement perceptible.
by_translator.weaknesses: Several local glosses introduce implications the editor should remove. At X30 the English ‘two eighths’ can suggest fractions or note values. At V39 the Russian makes the unnamed fraction’s smallness the cause of its having no name. At V42 D reports a printed 3 on a line whose three divisions can be counted but whose numeral is absent. At X56 and V64 the Russian specifies a farewell where the genre name establishes departure. At X32 ‘proportions’ blurs the distinction D established in the opening.

overall.summary: D is a frequent choice for running prose in both languages. Individual passages call for a different base, including A’s English at X13, B’s account of the fractional scale at V22, and C’s account of 8:3 at V42. Keep the two Latin arguments separately visible. Xylander supplies ordinary Latin interval names and glosses his terms for sounding alongside or opposite. Vinet introduces his two classes without those etymologies. X26 calls the interval species composite before X27 calls an individual interval incomposite, while V31 introduces the list as simple. The scale examples also require a distinction between operations. Starting from eight, adding one half or one quarter of a unit gives the ratios 17:16 and 33:32 to the initial length. Equal divisions of the musical interval 9:8 give its square root or fourth root. Finally, X34 gives an unnamed quantity smaller than a diesis, V39 explicitly calls it part of a tone, and V55 subsequently reckons the fourth without it. Preserve each statement and explain the tension in the commentary. The segment recommendations give separate choices for Russian and English wherever their merits differ.
